title: Illustrated Typography
slide_intent: Make lettering express the words it carries while fitting the available surface, so packaging communicates appetite and product difference at a glance.
strategic_value: Flame Bold caps transformed into compact food descriptions can give Burger King packages a consistent voice without identical shapes.
demonstration: The page pairs two stated packaging jobs with eight labeled lettering specimens: five small rounds, a larger round and two elongated formats, with selected inch dimensions.
practical_value: Start from Flame Bold caps, use descriptive words as visual cues and fit the lettering to the packaging shape.

content_islands.name: Lettering guidance
content_islands.spec: Place the Flame Bold caps basis and two packaging objectives in the left column.

content_islands.name: Upper specimens
content_islands.spec: Line up five compact circular two-word compositions with product-wrap captions; retain the 3.5-inch bracket.

content_islands.name: Lower specimens
content_islands.spec: Compare a 4-inch Hearty Melty round with Tasty Eggy and Tender Crispy elongated forms and their printed dimensions.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text states that packaging lettering should use descriptive words as visual cues and fill different packaging shapes.
reference_purposes.Expression: Eight examples distort the same base lettering into rounded and elongated compositions.
reference_purposes.Application: The page identifies Flame Bold caps as the base and labels the product-wrap examples and selected dimensions.

ingredient.name: Illustrated packaging typography
ingredient.role: Make descriptive food words visible through shape.
ingredient.application: Begin with Flame Bold caps; derive visual cues from the words and fill the intended packaging shape.
ingredient.scope: Historical packaging examples; printed inch dimensions describe the shown wraps, not a universal type-size formula.
